One board member, Mr. W. Gaines, Jr., mounted a proposed land use plan on each side of his truck and drove through the community meeting with individuals or groups to discuss the proposals and to get residents input. Another special committee, the Priorities Committee, reviews comments and proposals from Individuals or groups within the area to define community objectives and to develop priorities concerning those objectives.
When the general land use plan was developed the Special Program and Planning Committee began studying one square block discussing housing types and patterns. The objectives of the committee were to maintain approximately the same density, provide off-street parking, and create maximum useable open space. Detailed planning proposed closing some streets, changing the current grid system for streets, and revising traffic patterns to route heavy traffic around rather than through the community.
In September, 1961, a public meeting was held at the Glorious Church of God In Christ to give community citizens an opportunity to comment on the proposed redevelopment plans which had been developed by the RPSB. The plans proposed staged acquisition and demolition in designated areas with development of new housing, community facilities and recreation areas. Mr. J. L. Furman, Supervisor of Relocation for the Redevelopment and Housing Authority explained relocation assistance and benefits which will be available when the program is funded for execution. It was also announced at this meeting that HUD had allocated an additional 3.6 million dollars for execution of the program making the total grant reservation 13.5 million dollars.
In November, 1971, the West End Advisory Council, Inc., through the Richmond Community Action Program retained a planning consultant to review the Randolph land use plan. After limited review his report was submitted and forwarded to the RPSB for comment. In January, 1972, the RPSB replied to the West End Advisory Council and reminded the Council of the responsibilities and limitations of the program as well as the communities overall goals and objectives.
An issue resulted from a planning proposal involving land which is currently owned by the City for use as a cemetery. The proposal was to extend a street through the vacant cemetery land to connect to another street to allow non-community traffic to by-pass the community. Approximately 2 acres of unused cemetery land then would become available to the community for development of new housing. The matter was presented to the City Manager by the Redevelopment and Housing Authority and the RPSB for his review. At a meeting with the RPSB on December 7, 1971, the City Manager, Mr. Alan Kiepper, congratulated the RPSB on their thorough studies and agreed with their proposal for the new street alignment and to allow the 2 acres of unused cemetery land to be used for development of housing.
In January, 1972, a task force was designated from members of the Randolph Special Planning Committee to propose a location for development of a housing site for the elderly. The task force studied possible locations and proposed a site near the center of the community.
In January, 1972, a staff briefing of the Randolph plan was held for members of the Richmond Regional Planning District Commission (RRPDC), and on January 27, 1972, the plan was reviewed by the Commission. Members of the RPSB were present at that meeting and participated in presentation of the plan. The RRPDC approved the Randolph Plan at that meeting and congratulated members of the RPSB and the Randolph community for their participation in the planning effort.
